FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Sports & Movement flashcards.

Forty cards that turn the whole wide world of sport into active play a four-year-old can start today: the ball games every playground knows, the run-jump-throw heart of athletics, the water sports, the wheels and boards and ice, climbing and riding, the aim-and-precision games, the martial arts and one mighty lift. Every card is a gross motor skill with a name — and every name is a game the body already wants to play.

These cards belong to Class 37 · Sports, Movement & Play on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Tap any card to open it.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Sort the cards by how the body moves

    Ball games in one pile, water sports in another, wheels and boards and ice in a third. Sorting by movement IS fundamental movement skills practice — and every child sorts them a slightly different way, all of them right.

  2. 02

    Do the word, then name the word

    Pull a card, do the sport’s Big Move in the living room — a soccer kick, a gymnastics balance, a swimming reach — then say the name together. Gross motor first, vocabulary second: that is the order four-year-olds learn best.

  3. 03

    Pick a mini tournament

    Lay out six cards and let your child run a tiny sports day: one move from each card, a big cheer after every attempt and a drawn medal at the end. Physical literacy grows on reps, and reps grow on fun.

  4. 04

    Find the sport on screen or street

    Watch sixty seconds of any card’s sport or spot it on a walk — a bike, a net, a bat and ball in the park. Real-world matching turns forty cards into forty treasure hunts.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Soccer Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A player, a ball and a big open field — soccer is the first sport of almost every country on Earth, and the first one a four-year-old can actually play.

      Say it together

      “Soccer is kicking the ball with your feet — no hands allowed! You kick it to a friend, or into the big net for a goal.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Set two chair-legs as a goal across the room and take turns kicking a soft ball through. Then add the stop: kick, run, put one foot on top of the ball — freeze it. Stopping the ball is the secret skill of every good player.

      Quick parent note

      Feet-first sports are the friendliest entry into ball skills: the ball is big, the kick is a motion legs already know, and missing barely matters. In New Zealand and Australia it is called football too — same game, same joy.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Soccer lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Basketball Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A bouncing orange ball and a hoop up high — basketball is throw, bounce and catch, the three things small hands practise all day anyway.

      Say it together

      “Basketball is bouncing the ball with your hands and tossing it into the hoop. Bounce, bounce, throw — swish!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      A laundry basket on the floor is today’s hoop. Bounce the ball five times, then drop-toss it in. Move the basket further away each round. Every catch you take is hand-eye coordination doing push-ups.

      Quick parent note

      The bounce is the real teacher here: a ball that comes back up asks to be hit again, and hitting a moving ball on purpose is one of the big fundamental movement skills.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Basketball lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Volleyball Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A light ball and a high net — volleyball is a game of not letting the ball touch the ground, played by a team that talks in bumps and sets.

      Say it together

      “In volleyball we bump the ball up, up, up — and never let it touch the floor! Over the net to the other team, then back again.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Blow up a balloon and play keep-it-up over a string or a row of sofa cushions. Balloons hang in the air long enough for little arms to get under them — a proper bump before school even starts.

      Quick parent note

      A balloon or a soft beach ball first, a volleyball later: the skill being built is the underarm bump, and slow air buys the time small arms need to find it.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Volleyball lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Tennis Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A racket, a fuzzy yellow ball and a net down the middle — tennis is a rally: I hit, you hit, nobody lets it stop.

      Say it together

      “Tennis is hitting the ball with a racket — tap! — over the net to your friend, and they tap it back. How many taps can we do?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Balloon or soft ball, big spoon or paddle: tap it up, let it bounce, tap again. Count your record out loud. When the taps get steady, tap it across the sofa-back "net" to a partner.

      Quick parent note

      Start with something that hangs in the air and a hit-anything surface — the striking skill transfers straight to a real racket later. Strike-and-watch is the fundamental movement skill here.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Tennis lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Badminton Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Thinnest rackets, lightest tap — badminton sends a feathered shuttlecock floating over the net, slow as a soap bubble.

      Say it together

      “Badminton uses a shuttlecock — a little feather rocket! We tap it softly and it floats over the net like a parachute.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Toss a shuttlecock (or a lightweight sponge ball) and let your child tap it back up with the flat hand first, then a junior racket. Watch how it wobbles and floats — that drift is what makes badminton feel like catching a falling leaf.

      Quick parent note

      The shuttlecock’s slow float is a gift for young eyes: it stays catchable far longer than a ball, so tracking it trains the same eye skill every ball sport needs.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Badminton lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Table Tennis Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A low net on a big table and a ball that goes ping — table tennis is tennis shrunk down to kitchen-table size.

      Say it together

      “Table tennis is ping pong! The little ball bounces on the table and we hit it with small paddles — ping, pong, ping!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Kneel at the table and bounce the ball on your paddle: how many bounces in a row? Then bounce it once on your side and tap it over the books-as-net. Fast little bounces make fast little eyes.

      Quick parent note

      The small court keeps everything within one arm’s reach, which makes it a brilliant first rally game — the ball always comes back somewhere gettable.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Table Tennis lesson on the Learning Path.

      Baseball Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Bat, ball and four white bases in a big green diamond — baseball is hit the ball, run the loop, come home.

      Say it together

      “Baseball is hitting the ball with a bat — CRACK! — then running around the bases all the way back home. Safe!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Balance a soft ball on a stool or a tee, swing a plastic bat or a rolled sock, and run your own diamond of cushions. Then trade turns: one pitches gently, one catches with the big glove. Hit, run, catch — the whole sport in a corridor.

      Quick parent note

      Off a tee is how every hitter starts, big leagues included — the swing is the skill, and the tee lets little hands meet the ball instead of chasing it.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Baseball lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Cricket Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Flat bat, three wooden stumps and a big field — cricket is the game of the long afternoon: bowl it, hit it, run, and the other team fetches.

      Say it together

      “Cricket is hitting the ball with a flat bat — whack! — while the wickets stand behind you. Then we run! The other team fetches the ball.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Stand three paper-towel tubes as wickets, bowl a soft ball with a big gentle underarm roll, and swing the flat bat straight through the line. Whoever hits it gets to run; whoever fields it brings it back. Backyard cricket needs nothing else.

      Quick parent note

      Underarm bowling first — it arrives slowly enough to swing at, and the straight full swing it teaches is the stroke every cricketer keeps forever.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cricket lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Rugby Flashcard for Preschoolers

      An oval ball hugged in both arms and a wide green field — rugby is run forward, pass backward, fall down, get up, laugh.

      Say it together

      “In rugby we hold the ball with BOTH hands and run as fast as we can — but we can only pass it backwards to our friends!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Jog around the garden hugging a cushion "ball" in both arms, and on your call, pass it backwards over the shoulder to the runner behind. Forward-run, back-pass is the whole sport’s rhythm, played at four-year-old speed.

      Quick parent note

      The backwards pass feels upside-down at first — and that little brain-twister is exactly why children love it. Tag versions (rippa, touch) make it the friendliest running game on the card wall.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Rugby lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      American Football Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The pointed brown ball that refuses to bounce straight — American football is run the play, throw long, and cross the line for a touchdown.

      Say it together

      “This is American football — the funny egg-shaped ball! We throw it far to a friend, or hug it tight and run to the end zone. Touchdown!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Two cushions one room apart are the end zones. Take turns: hug the ball and run the "field", or point your fingers and throw it across. The oval ball flies funny — that wobble is the joke, and catching it is the skill.

      Quick parent note

      Throwing an oval ball teaches the over-arm throw at its very best: fingers behind, arm over the top, step as you throw — the same pattern every ball sport borrows.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the American Football lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Hockey Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A bent stick, a puck that slides, and a goal to fill — hockey is the fastest team game on Earth, played on ice or on the street.

      Say it together

      “Hockey is pushing the puck with a stick — dribble, dribble, SHOOT! Into the goal it goes.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      A sponge or paper ball is the puck, a broom or pool noodle is the stick. Dribble it around chair-cones, then shoot between the sofa-legs. On the floor nobody falls, and the dribbling skill is the same one the big ice players drill.

      Quick parent note

      Keep the stick low and the puck slow: floor hockey builds the side-to-side stick work that transfers to field hockey, ice hockey and even golf swings later.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Hockey lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Lacrosse Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A stick with a net pocket at the end — lacrosse is the old, fast game of catching the ball in the stick and carrying it like a nest.

      Say it together

      “Lacrosse sticks have a little net basket! We scoop the ball up, hold it in the net, and run — then throw it to a friend.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      A small net bag, a scooper or even a large spoon: scoop a soft ball off the floor, jog a lap without dropping it, then toss it into a bucket. Scooping off the ground is a genuine catching skill — from below.

      Quick parent note

      Lacrosse flips catching upside-down: the net catches from underneath. Children who struggle with hand-catches often shine here — the stick does the catching while the eyes learn to track.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Lacrosse lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Handball Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Run, bounce, jump and fling — handball is what happens when basketball and soccer share a court and the goal is your own two hands.

      Say it together

      “Handball is throwing the ball into the goal with your HAND — no stick, no bat, just a big strong throw!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      A soft ball and a doorway or cushion goal: take three giant steps, throw with one arm, then swap and be the goalkeeper with arms up wide. Three steps, one throw, one cheer — repeat until dinner.

      Quick parent note

      One-armed goal-throwing is the strongest throwing pattern in sport, and the keeper role makes missing fun — every save gets the same roar as every goal.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Handball lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Golf Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The smallest ball, the biggest grass — golf is swing slow, hit straight, and count how many taps it takes to land in the hole.

      Say it together

      “Golf is hitting the tiny ball into the tiny hole — swing slow and smooth, like brushing the grass. One… two… three taps!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      A bucket, a spoon and a pom-pom: tap the pom-pom across the carpet to the bucket in as few taps as you can. Count out loud together. The counting IS the game — golf quietly teaches numbers while it teaches aim.

      Quick parent note

      Golf is the aiming sport: small target, slow swing, big patience. It grows the controlled-strike end of fundamental movement skills — the opposite lesson from the hockey whack.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Golf lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Athletics Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Fast legs, long jumps, mighty throws — athletics is track and field: the three things every human body learns first, done as sport.

      Say it together

      “Athletics is running, jumping and throwing — the Olympic games! Run to the line, jump as far as you can, throw it far, far away!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Chalk three stations on the pavement: a sprint line ("run fast!"), a long-jump line ("bend knees, jump!"), and a bean-bag throw ("big arm, throw!"). One minute each, big cheer, next station. That is a real athletics meet, kid-size.

      Quick parent note

      Run, jump, throw — New Zealand schools literally teach these three words as the heart of fundamental movement skills, and every athletics event is one of them done bigger.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Athletics lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Gymnastics Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Balance beams, big mats and bodies that make shapes — gymnastics is the sport of controlling exactly what your body does.

      Say it together

      “Gymnastics is balancing and rolling and making shapes with your body — arms out, one foot up… hold it, hold it… and ta-da!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Balance on one foot like a flamingo for five slow counts, then do a log roll across the bed or a mat, then hold a "star shape" — arms and legs wide. Balance, roll, shape: a full gymnastics class in the living room.

      Quick parent note

      Balance is the quiet king of all sport skills — every other card on this wall borrows it. Gymnastics trains it on purpose, which is why gymnasts learn every other sport fast.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Gymnastics lesson on the Learning Path.

      Marathon Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Forty-two kilometres, one step at a time — the marathon is the longest race of all, where the win is simply keeping going.

      Say it together

      “A marathon is a SUPER long running race — so long it takes all day! You do not rush; you keep stepping, one foot, other foot, all the way.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play marathon around the house or the block: instead of speed, count laps together. Ten laps earns a water break and a medal drawing. The lesson of the marathon is pacing — slow and steady really does win.

      Quick parent note

      Four-year-olds are natural sprinters and terrible pacers, which is exactly why the marathon is a fun card: it teaches the opposite trick — steady beats speedy when the road is long.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Marathon lesson on the Learning Path.

      Triathlon Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Swim, then bike, then run — no pause, no nap: the triathlon is three sports stacked into one giant race.

      Say it together

      “Tri means THREE! A triathlon is three races in one — first swim, then ride your bike, then run to the finish. Nobody stops in between!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Living-room triathlon: crawl across the sofa-sea (swim), ride the hobby-horse or trike loop (bike), sprint to the finish cushion (run). Announce each leg like a race commentator. Three sports, one medal.

      Quick parent note

      Switching skills mid-game — from crawling to pedalling to sprinting — is a genuine coordination workout, and the made-up race format makes reps feel like a party.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Triathlon lesson on the Learning Path.

      Cycling Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Two wheels, round pedals and the wind in your face — cycling is the first machine a small person gets to drive all by themselves.

      Say it together

      “Cycling is riding your bike — helmet on first! Push the pedals round and round, and off you go down the path.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Practise the pedalling motion lying on the back, legs cycling the air — round and round, not up and down. Then helmet on, and out to the path or trike. The air-cycling game makes the real pedals feel already-known.

      Quick parent note

      Helmets are non-negotiable from the very first ride — the safety habit starts with training wheels, and a helmet worn at four is a helmet worn at fourteen.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cycling lesson on the Learning Path.

      Swimming Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Arms reaching, legs kicking, bubbles blowing — swimming is the sport that is also a life skill, and the one kids would do every single day if allowed.

      Say it together

      “Swimming is moving through the water — kick kick, reach reach, blow bubbles! And we NEVER swim without a grown-up.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      On dry land first: lie on the tummy and do big arm circles ("windmill arms!") and fast flutter kicks. In the bath, blow bubbles with the mouth in the water. All three pieces are real swimming strokes waiting for the pool.

      Quick parent note

      The safety line belongs on every repetition: never swim without a grown-up, never reach into water alone. The card teaches the fun and says the rule in the same breath.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Swimming lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      Diving Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Hands together, body straight as a pencil — diving is the art of entering the water so neatly the splash is tiny.

      Say it together

      “Diving is jumping into the water hands first, straight as a pencil — arms squeeze the ears, toes pointed, SPLASH (a small one!).”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Practise the diver’s body on the carpet: arms up squeezing the ears, body tall, tip-toes, hold the pencil shape for three counts — then fall forward like a tree into the "water" (the sofa). The shape is the skill; the water can wait.

      Quick parent note

      The pencil shape does double duty: it is the diving entry AND the posture every jump and vault borrows. Small splash, big pride.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Diving lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Water Polo Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A team in the water, a ball in the air — water polo is soccer played while floating, with throws instead of kicks.

      Say it together

      “Water polo is throwing the ball into the goal while you float — legs kick underneath like an egg-beater, hands pass the ball to friends!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Practise the egg-beater sit: in the bath or shallow pool, sit upright and whirl the legs, arms sculling out to the sides. Then toss a soft ball to a partner — water polo passes are throws, one hand, aim at their chest.

      Quick parent note

      Treading water is the hidden swimming super-skill — hands busy with the ball, legs do all the floating. It is also one of the four things swim schools teach before strokes.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Water Polo lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Surfing Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A board under the feet and the whole ocean pushing — surfing is standing up on moving water and riding it to the beach.

      Say it together

      “Surfing is standing on a board on the wave — paddle, paddle, POP UP! Knees bent, arms out, ride it all the way in!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Pop-up practice on the carpet: lie flat, hands under shoulders, jump the feet in and stand low in one hop — that is the surfer’s pop-up. Then balance on a cushion or a wobbly board, knees soft, arms wide. Pop up, stand tall, repeat.

      Quick parent note

      The pop-up is the whole sport in one move, and practising it on the floor is what real surf schools do first. Balance plus a dash of bravery — the ocean does the rest.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Surfing lesson on the Learning Path.

      Rowing Flashcard for Preschoolers

      One long thin boat, everyone facing backwards, all oars pulling as one — rowing is the team sport where nobody sees the finish line coming.

      Say it together

      “Rowing is pulling the oars to move the boat — lean forward, pull back, glide! Everyone rows together, in the same rhythm: dip, pull, glide.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Sit on the floor facing a partner, hold a towel or stick between you and row: both lean forward, both pull back, counting "dip — pull — glide". In-time pulling is the actual skill of a crew — the boat only moves when everybody moves together.

      Quick parent note

      Rowing is the togetherness card: strength matters less than rhythm. It is also a rare pulling sport — most ball games push and throw, the boat teaches the pull.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Canoeing Flashcard for Preschoolers

      An open boat, a single paddle and calm water — canoeing is the quiet sport: dip the paddle, pull, and the lake carries you along.

      Say it together

      “Canoeing is paddling a boat with one paddle — dip it on the left, then the right, and the canoe goes straight ahead!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Sit cross-legged on the floor holding a mop or a rolled poster as a paddle, and "paddle" a rug-boat: big reach, long pull, left side, right side. Then ask: what happens if you only paddle ONE side? (You spin in a circle!)

      Quick parent note

      The left-right paddling rule is a real physics lesson in disguise — one-side-only paddling is how you steer. Calm water, life jacket, grown-up: the card’s three quiet rules.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Canoeing lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Sailing Flashcard for Preschoolers

      No engine, no paddles — just a big white sail catching the wind: sailing is the sport of letting the sky do the pushing.

      Say it together

      “Sailing is letting the WIND push the boat! The big white sail catches the wind like a kite, and the boat slides across the water.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Be the boat: hold a pillow or towel "sail" to your chest and walk only where a partner blows or fans you — move toward the "wind" and you stop; angle across it and you glide. That wind-angle game is real sailing thinking.

      Quick parent note

      Sailing teaches reading invisible things — wind you cannot see, only feel. It is science class on water, which is why sailors always end up explaining the weather.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Sailing lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Skating Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Shiny blades, smooth ice and the wobbliest eight metres in sport — skating is learning to glide: push, and the ice carries you.

      Say it together

      “Skating is gliding on the ice — little steps first, then stand still and LET the ice carry you. Wobbly knees are doing it right!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Slipper-skate at home: socks on a smooth floor, take skating steps, then freeze and glide as far as the momentum goes. Practise the soft fall too — knees down, hands on knees, giggle. Every skater falls; good skaters fall soft.

      Quick parent note

      The glide is the magic moment — the first time the ice (or the hallway floor) carries the child without stepping. Helmets for real ice, socks for the hallway, patience for both.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Skating lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Skiing Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Long boards on white snow and a mountain going down — skiing is pointing the tips together, bending the knees and letting the hill teach you.

      Say it together

      “Skiing is sliding down the snow on long boards! Tips together like a pizza slice to slow down… tips straight like french fries to go fast!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Snowplough practice in socks: slide one foot out till the heels nearly meet — the "pizza" wedge — then slide them parallel again, "french fries". Do it down a carpet slope holding your hands. The stop comes before the speed; that is the mountain’s rule.

      Quick parent note

      Pizza and french fries are what every ski school in the world calls the wedge and the parallel slide — and the fact that four-year-olds remember it forever says everything about naming a skill after lunch.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Skiing lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Curling Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A big polished stone, a sheet of ice and two friends sweeping like mad — curling is bowls on ice, the gentlest loud sport there is.

      Say it together

      “Curling is sliding a big smooth stone on the ice toward the rings — and your friends sweep the ice in front to make it go further! Sweep sweep sweep!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Kitchen curling: slide a plastic lid or a bean bag across the smooth floor toward a paper-plate target, and let the "sweepers" fan the floor in front of it with a tea towel. The sweeping genuinely helps — and that is the joke.

      Quick parent note

      Curling is the aiming card wearing a team jersey: the slide aims, but the sweepers decide how far. No other sport lets your friends change your throw after you let go.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Curling lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Skateboarding Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A board with four small wheels and a pavement — skateboarding is standing sideways on a rolling board and making the street your playground.

      Say it together

      “Skateboarding is riding a board on little wheels — foot up front, push with the back foot, knees bent, and roll!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Balance practice first: stand on a board (or a cushion) on carpet, feet sideways, knees soft, arms out — hold the stance for five counts. Then one gentle push on a smooth, flat surface with helmet and pads on. Stance on carpet, roll on pavement.

      Quick parent note

      Sideways stance is what makes a skateboard feel strange at first — the body faces where the board is not going. The carpet-stance game fixes that fear before the wheels ever move.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Skateboarding lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Climbing Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Colourful holds up a tall wall — climbing is the thinking sport: where does the hand go next, and which foot gets you there?

      Say it together

      “Climbing is going UP the wall with your hands and feet — grip, reach, plan the next hold… and always, always come back down slow.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Hallway climbing wall: tape paper "holds" at climbing heights, touch them in order — red, blue, red — without lifting the feet off the floor. Then climb the real playground ladder or wall with hands and feet planning together. Up slow, down slower.

      Quick parent note

      Climbing is cross-lateral thinking: right hand with left foot, planning three moves ahead. It builds grip strength, sequencing and the calm kind of bravery — and the down is as trained as the up.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Climbing lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Horse Riding Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A pony, a helmet and the best seat in sport — riding is asking a large kind animal to carry you, politely, sitting very tall.

      Say it together

      “Horse riding is sitting on a pony and riding with gentle hands — sit tall, heels down, and hold the reins soft as holding a baby bird.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Practise the rider’s seat on a cushion-horse: sit tall, pretend reins in soft fists, heels down, and do the rising trot — up-down, up-down — while a partner counts. Gentle hands are the whole secret; ponies listen to soft fingers.

      Quick parent note

      Riding is a partnership sport: the helmet is non-negotiable, the calm voice matters as much as the seat, and the pony is a teammate with opinions — which is why riders learn patience first.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Horse Riding lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Archery Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A curved bow, a straight arrow and a far round target — archery is the quietest aiming sport: breathe out, hold steady, let go gently.

      Say it together

      “Archery is shooting an arrow at the target with a bow — stand side-on, pull the string slow, aim… and let go softly. Bullseye!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Suction-cup bow or a rubber-band shooter, paper-plate target on a chair: the game is the routine, not the hit — stand side-on, draw slow, hold for one breath, release soft. Bullseye or not, a calm routine is the skill archery teaches.

      Quick parent note

      Slow is the whole sport: the arrow goes exactly where the steady hand and the quiet breath put it. Real ranges have real rules — arrow up only when everyone is behind the line, always.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Archery lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Bowling Flashcard for Preschoolers

      One heavy ball, ten white pins and a shiny wooden lane — bowling is the roll-straight-and-count sport, and everyone’s first birthday-party favourite.

      Say it together

      “Bowling is rolling the ball down the lane to knock over the pins — roll it slow along the floor… CRASH! How many fell down?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Water-bottle pins at the end of the hallway, any mid-size ball: the rule is ROLL, never throw — one hand underneath, push the ball along the floor. Then count the fallen pins together. Rolling straight is the skill; the counting is the maths class hiding inside.

      Quick parent note

      Underneath-rolling is a genuine gross motor skill most sports never teach — and bowling is the only one where the pins do the cheering for you.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bowling lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Fencing Flashcard for Preschoolers

      White suits, wire masks and thin swords that bend — fencing is chess at the speed of lightning: poke before you are poked.

      Say it together

      “Fencing is a sword game with masks on — en garde! Advance, retreat… LUNGE! The tip of your sword touches the jacket and scores a point.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Foam-sword duel with pool noodles: masks optional, manners mandatory — en garde stance (side-on, knees bent, sword up), three advances forward, three retreats back, then one big lunge at a cushion target. Footwork first, poking never at people.

      Quick parent note

      Fencing footwork is the hidden treasure: side-on stance, quick small steps, balance held while moving fast — the same footwork fencers, boxers and tennis players all borrow.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Fencing lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Boxing Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Big gloves, a strong stance and fast straight punches — boxing is the sport of hitting pads, dodging well and standing your ground.

      Say it together

      “Boxing is punching with big gloves — hands up protecting your face, feet planted, jab jab at the pads! We punch PADS, never people.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Grown-up holds cushions as pads: jab-jab-cross with the little fists, three rounds of thirty seconds, feet bouncing lightly. The golden rule lives on the card: pads and punching bags only, never at people, never at pets, never at walls.

      Quick parent note

      Done right, boxing for little ones is pad-work fitness — stance, guard, straight punches and the discipline of where punching is allowed. The rule IS the lesson.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Boxing lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Judo Flashcard for Preschoolers

      White suits on soft mats and the gentlest name in sport — judo means "the gentle way": grip, balance, and let your partner down softly.

      Say it together

      “Judo is the GENTLE way — we grip the jacket, keep our balance, and if we fall, we fall soft like a starfish. The mat is our friend!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Break-fall practice on a bed or mat: sit, roll back, arms slap out wide — slap! Then the jacket grip: hold a partner’s sleeve and elbow, step around, both keep balance. Falling soft and gripping gentle are judo’s two first skills.

      Quick parent note

      Every martial art starts with respect — the bow, the partner, the mat — and judo adds the world’s most useful safety skill: knowing how to fall without hurt, learned at four, kept for life.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Judo lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Karate Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A white suit, a coloured belt and punches that stop in the air — karate is the empty-hand way: strong blocks, straight punches, and manners first.

      Say it together

      “Karate means "empty hand" — no weapons, just your body! Block strong, punch straight, and ALWAYS bow to your partner first.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Kata in the living room: bow, then four moves in a line — low block, middle block, high block, straight punch — counting in a big voice: ichi, ni, san, shi! (That is one, two, three, four in Japanese.) Blocks before punches, always.

      Quick parent note

      Karate’s secret is that it is a manners programme wearing a punch: the counting, the bowing, the stopping-in-the-air control are the actual curriculum, and four-year-olds earn belts for exactly that.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Karate lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Sports, Movement & Play (Class 37) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Taekwondo Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The kicking martial art — taekwondo is fast feet: high kicks, quick hops and pads that go thwack.

      Say it together

      “Taekwondo is the kicking sport from Korea — front kick, side kick, roundhouse! Fast feet, strong legs, and we kick PADS, never people.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Pad-kick drill: a cushion held by the grown-up at knee height — front kick, kick, kick! Then a tiny hop and turn for the side kick. Ten kicks each leg, big count-out-loud. Kicking high asks for balance, which is why taekwondo legs are springy.

      Quick parent note

      Kicking trains balance on one leg better than almost any game — and the pad rule (pads, never people) is stated on every card and in every dojang in the world.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Taekwondo lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Weightlifting Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The strongest people in the Olympics bend and lift a heavy barbell clean overhead — weightlifting is the sport of strength, done slowly and safely.

      Say it together

      “Weightlifting is lifting heavy things with strong muscles and a straight back — bend the knees, hold tight, lift… UP! The strongest lifters in the world do this.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Soft-barbell lift: a pool noodle with two socks for plates — feet apart, bend the KNEES (not the back), hold wide, stand tall, press overhead, big cheer, lower slow. Five lifts, then re-stack the "plates". The knees-bend rule is the whole lesson — it is how weightlifters protect their backs forever.

      Quick parent note

      For four-year-olds this card is really about the safe-lifting pattern — bend the knees, straight back, hold close — the same rule they will use carrying school bags and grocery bags for the rest of their lives.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Weightlifting lesson on the Learning Path.
